title: The Largest XOR of a Subarray With At Least L Elements

concept.title: The XOR of a subarray is the XOR of two prefix values: insert the allowed prefixes into a binary trie and ask for the best partner
body: Among all subarrays with **at least `L` elements**, find the largest XOR of their elements. For `8 1 2 12 7` and `L = 2` the answer is 15: the subarray `1 2 12` has the XOR `1 ^ 2 ^ 12 = 15`. The brute force over all O(n^2) subarrays is too slow for 30000 numbers.

Let `P[i]` be the XOR of the first `i` numbers (`P[0] = 0`). The XOR of the subarray from `j + 1` to `i` is `P[i] ^ P[j]`, and the length is `i - j`. So we want the largest `P[i] ^ P[j]` over pairs with `i - j >= L`. For every `i`, the partners `j` are the prefixes with index `0 .. i - L`, a set that only **grows** when `i` grows: insert `P[i - L]` before handling `i`.

body.code:
P = prefix XORs, P[0] = 0
best = 0
for i in range(L, n + 1):
    insert(P[i - L])              # the prefix P[i - L] becomes an allowed partner
    best = max(best, query(P[i])) # the largest P[i] ^ P[j] over the allowed partners j

body: The structure that finds the partner maximising the XOR with a given number is a **binary trie** of 30 levels: `insert(x)` follows the bits of `x` from the top and creates the missing nodes; `query(y)` walks down and, at each level, prefers the child with the **opposite** bit (it puts a 1 in the result); if that child does not exist it takes the other one. Each operation costs 30 steps, so the whole program is O(30 n). The trie has at most `30 (n + 1) + 1` nodes.

statement: A list of `n` numbers and a number `L` are given. Among all subarrays (consecutive parts) with at least `L` elements find the largest XOR of the elements, and print it.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `L`: the number of values and the smallest allowed length.

examples.note: The subarray 1 2 12 has the XOR 15, the largest among the subarrays with at least 2 elements.

hints: Use prefix XORs: the XOR of a subarray is P[i] ^ P[j].
For position i the allowed partners are P[0], ..., P[i - L].
Keep the allowed prefixes in a binary trie and walk it preferring opposite bits.
